blocks.text: Start with the exact failing action and its time. Use Computer Management → System & Recovery → Maintenance & Health → Services & Logs to inspect relevant services. Application output may use managed rsyslog sinks separately from the journal; absence in journal is not proof of no error.

Review logs locally before sharing them. Remove credentials, usernames, addresses, hostnames, document titles, private paths and raw network/device identifiers. Help displays documentation only and never reads or copies journal text.

Some installed profiles use transient log/cache storage. Reboot can remove useful evidence. Preserve a private sanitized excerpt before reboot when practical. Journal vacuum and log deletion remove evidence and require deliberate authorization.

Include the component and exact menu action, the time, what you expected, what appeared, and whether the failure repeats. Distinguish a missing command, a rejected configuration, an authorization denial and a request whose result is uncertain. A screenshot of a blank window alone rarely identifies the cause.

Keep the smallest relevant local excerpt. Preserve a reported recovery path when a tool cannot prove restoration, and do not repeat a mutation with an unknown outcome. Guide titles and commands in Help are reference material; the app does not attach logs or send a report anywhere.
